pages.title: ADR 0001: New repository and naming

pages.description: AGPL-3.0, clean-room with respect to the GPL-3 upstream.

pages.title: ADR 0003: Core application stack
pages.description: TypeScript, Hono, Vite, TanStack Router, Tailwind 4; Next.js rejected pending the memory spike.

pages.title: ADR 0004: Two tiers — a hardware daemon and a core
pages.description: One hardware daemon (hald) and one core, joined by a versioned contract; deployment topologies.

pages.title: ADR 0005: tRPC as the primary control plane; MCP, REST and MQTT are additive
pages.description: tRPC first; REST, MCP, MQTT, SSE and WebSocket are generated or additive surfaces.

pages.title: ADR 0006: Rust for the hardware daemon
pages.description: Why the hardware daemon is Rust (rppal, cross-compiled) rather than Python/gpiozero.

pages.title: ADR 0009: Pump safety guard and latched faults
pages.description: Pump duty clamp, bounded runs, dry-run interlock, over-temp cutoff and latched faults; amended 2026-11-14 for full duty, the brown-out and current guards, and hal.toml-only guard settings.

pages.title: ADR 0010: Drizzle ORM + SQLite behind a Store interface
pages.description: One SQLite file via drizzle on the unit; an in-memory Store with identical semantics for tests and the browser demo.

pages.title: ADR 0011: MCP tool design and Model Hardware Standard alignment
pages.description: Tools are named read/write primitives with units and declared limits over the tRPC caller; refusals are errors.

pages.title: ADR 0012: Deployment and trust model
pages.description: Tarball releases with hald binaries, systemd units, LAN-only trust with an opt-in API key.

pages.title: ADR 0013: Core-level MQTT bridge for Home Assistant
pages.description: An additive MQTT client for grow reminders, cycle state, light hours and a bounded water button; the daemon already publishes the physical entities.

pages.title: ADR 0014: Auto-dosing safety
pages.description: Dosing pumps get their own guard with hard daily volume caps and lockouts; off by default.

pages.title: ADR 0015: Event bus and mutation broadcast
pages.description: One process-wide bus carries HAL events and mutations to SSE, WebSocket, the recorder and the HA bridge.

pages.title: ADR 0016: Shared design language with sleepypod
pages.description: Tokens, ds/ and ui/ ported verbatim with domain renames; extraction to a shared package deferred.

pages.title: ADR 0017: iOS client — reuse sleepypod's transport, not its app
pages.description: Evaluation of forking sleepypod/ios's networking layer against seedypod's tRPC router, and what core must add first.

pages.title: ADR 0018: Runtime sensor inventory
pages.description: Probes are added from the app through SensorKind descriptors; app-added sensors live in a state-dir overlay and go live without restarting hald.

pages.description: Vision analysers are an interface; their outputs share one versioned results table, export as a dataset, and can be mirrored to opt-in off-device storage and compute.

pages.title: Implementation plan (Phase 0 → 1.0)
pages.description: Phased build plan with parallelism markers, ADR index, HAL contract draft and OKRs.

headings.title: 0. Ground truth (what we know going in)
0.2 Safety invariants (lifted from upstream’s bug list — these are the spec, not nice-to-haves)
1.1 Repository layout (single repo, mirrors sleepypod/core + its modules/ multi-language precedent)
Phase 1 — Hardware reconnaissance & root ⏱ ½ day hands-on ∥ Phase 0 (fully independent)
Phase 2 — HAL (Rust daemon) ⏱ 1–2 weeks ⛔ Phase 1.6 (pin map) · Phase 0.6 (CI)
Phase 3 — Core (tRPC / scheduler / DB / MCP) ⏱ 1–2 weeks ⛔ Phase 2.1 (contract) · ∥ Phase 2.2–2.10
Phase 5 — Integrations ⏱ 3–5 days ⛔ Phase 3 · tasks ∥ each other
Phase 6 — Hardware expansion ⏱ 1–2 weekends ⛔ Phase 2 · ∥ Phases 4–5
Phase 7 — Plant intelligence (CV) ⏱ open-ended ⛔ 6.1 (compute) or off-device inference · ∥ Phase 5
4. ADR index (sleepypod template: Status/Date, Context, Decision, Consequences, References, Authors)
6. OKRs (first quarter) — new for this project; sleepypod has no OKR docs, only ADRs + knowledge/ (OKF)
7. Open questions (answer before the phase that needs them)
